item.title: Middle East war live: UAE responds to Iranian attacks as fragile ceasefire is challenged
item.description: The United Arab Emirates on Friday said it was responding to missile and drone attacks launched by Iran, hours after the US and the Islamic republic traded fire, further straining a fragile ceasefire. Iran and the US are trading blows as their negotiators are seeking a deal to end the fighting, but so far they’ve avoided a return to all-out fighting. Follow our liveblog for the latest updates.

item.title: Israel and Hezbollah continue to trade blows despite the ceasefire
item.description: Israel has taken responsibility for Wednesday night's strike on the southern suburbs of Beirut, with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu saying he personally authorised the attack to kill a top Hezbollah Commander identified as Malek Balou. The continued ceasefire incursions are further pressuring talks between Tel Aviv and Beirut, which are being supported by the US. item.title: Iran War Live Updates: Tehran Accuses U.S. of ‘Reckless’ Attacks After Exchange of Fire in Strait
item.description: Iran’s foreign minister said that the United States was undermining diplomacy, as Iranian officials said that Washington and Tehran were debating a peace proposal. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said that a response from Iran was expected on Friday.

item.title: Israel Says It Killed a Hezbollah Chief Near Beirut, Testing the Truce
item.description: The strike was the first near the Lebanese capital since a cease-fire that has curbed fighting but not halted it. Washington is pushing for a lasting peace, hoping it will ease diplomacy with Iran.

item.title: The U.S. awaits Iran's response as the UAE reports another missile barrage
item.description: The Iran war's shaky ceasefire was further strained on Friday as the United Arab Emirates responded to a missile and drone strikes.

item.title: Iran on the verge of economic asphyxiation -- rare footage from Tehran
item.description: Two months ago, Donald Trump claimed the United States would liberate the Iranian people when it launched the offensive alongside Israel. Two months into the war, the regime is still there, the repression continues, and the country stands on the verge of economic asphyxiation. Our colleagues at France 2 had the rare opportunity to film the lives of Iranians in the heart of Tehran, where runaway inflation has led to a cost of living crisis.

item.title: US military says it intercepted Iranian attacks in Strait of Hormuz
item.description: On Thursday, the US and Iran exchanged accusations and fire in the Strait of Hormuz, with Washington saying it intercepted Iranian attacks and struck back at military targets, while Tehran reported retaliatory action and rising regional tensions. The fragile ceasefire faced fresh strain amid widening conflict risks.

item.title: U.S. intercepts Iranian attacks on 3 ships. And, what to know about hantavirus
item.description: The U.S. says it intercepted Iranian attacks yesterday targeting three Navy ships. And, what to know about the hantavirus outbreak that started on a cruise ship.

item.title: Iran and the US trade fire over Hormuz, Trump says ceasefire still in effect
item.description: A new exchange of fire between Iran and the US occurred late Thursday night in the Strait of Hormuz, with both countries accusing each other of firing first. The latest by Simon Moritz.

item.title: Photo shows Israeli soldier desecrating Virgin Mary statue in Lebanon
item.description: The Israeli military says it has launched an investigation after a photo showing one of its soldiers desecrating a statue of the Virgin Mary in south Lebanon went viral, as he placed a cigarette into the statue's mouth whilst smoking. The IDF said it "respects freedom of religion" and that the soldier will be disciplined. The incident took place in Debel, the same village where an Israeli soldier was filmed last month smashing a Jesus statue with a sledgehammer.
